articles.title: Animais vítimas de caça e maus-tratos retornam à natureza no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerca de 4 mil animais de diferentes espécies foram reintroduzidos ao habitat natural em uma área de mata localizada no Sul do Espírito Santo.
articles.summary: Cerca de 4 mil animais, de diferentes espécies, já foram reintroduzidos ao habitat natural nessa área de mata no Sul do Espírito Santo.
articles.body:
Aves, jabutis, ouriços e macacos-prego resgatados de maus-tratos, caça e cativeiro ilegal ganharam uma nova chance de viver na natureza no Espírito Santo. Desde 2011, cerca de 4 mil animais já foram reintroduzidos ao habitat natural nessa área do Sul do estado.

Os animais passaram por tratamento, recuperação e um período de adaptação antes de serem reintroduzidos em uma área de Mata Atlântica preservada no Sul do estado.

O local exato da soltura foi mantido em sigilo por segurança. A medida evita que caçadores sejam atraídos para a região e que os animais voltem a ser capturados ilegalmente.

A ação foi realizada por equipes do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama), do Centro de Triagem de Animais Silvestres (Cetas) e do Centro de Reintrodução de Animais Silvestres (Cereias).

No Cetas, em Aracruz , no Norte do estado, os animais resgatados, apreendidos ou entregues voluntariamente passam por um longo período de recuperação.

Segundo o analista ambiental do Ibama e chefe do Cetas, Joseano Torezani, alguns animais chegam em condições muito ruins.

"A gaiola chega com muita sujeira, fezes misturada com comida e sem água. A gente tem que fazer um trabalho de profilaxia para tratar possíveis doenças e evitar a disseminação para aqueles que estão bem, e esse trabalho pode levar meses", explicou.

De volta à natureza: aves, jabutis, ouriços e macacos-prego vítimas de caça e maus-tratos são soltos na Mata Atlântica no Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

No Cereias, também em Aracruz, os animais passam por um período de readaptação antes de serem considerados aptos a voltar para a natureza.

"O Cereias recebe animais do estado todo, tanto apreendido quanto entrega voluntária, recolhimento. A gente trabalha comportamento, readaptação comportamental e alimentar também, devido ao longo período que passaram em cativeiro", destacou o biólogo José da Penha Rodrigues.

Antes da soltura, os animais são observados diariamente. A equipe avalia se eles conseguem se afastar das pessoas e dos tratadores e se já estão preparados para viver sem ajuda.

"No momento que ele vai se distanciando das pessoas, dos tratadores, de tudo, vai se afugentando, e o momento que ele está apto. E quando a gente chega perto do viveiro, e ele vem topar com a gente, conseguimos perceber que ele ainda está bem domesticado", explicou José da Penha.

Uma das etapas que pode levar mais tempo ocorre quando os animais chegam ao centro com as penas danificadas. Nesses casos, a recuperação pode levar meses ou até anos. Vinte papagaios da espécie chauá estão em um dos viveiros para, em breve, serem reintroduzidos na mata. O Espírito Santo concentra a maior população da espécie.

"Demanda muito tempo para eles fazerem a muda. São seis meses, um ano e, dependendo do caso, até um ano e meio ou dois anos", explicou o presidente do Cereias.

A readaptação também inclui o convívio com outros animais da mesma espécie. É o caso dos papagaios que passaram muitos anos isolados em cativeiro.

"Um papagaio que viveu a vida inteira sozinho, dez, 15, 20 anos, quando a gente junta com outros papagaios, é incrível como eles se reconhecem e começam a se comunicar. Eles podem até acasalar naquele momento, formar um par, que é para a vida inteira", contou.

No viveiro de adaptação, 20 papagaios-chauá aguardam o momento de serem reintroduzidos na mata. O Espírito Santo concentra a maior população da espécie.

Segundo o presidente do Cereias, a reprodução é importante para a conservação dos animais.

"É para ter aquela serventia para a natureza, que é passar os genes para frente. Enquanto que, se tivesse preso na casa da pessoa, seria um animal morto para a natureza", afirmou.

Animais ajudam no equilíbrio da natureza

A volta dos animais também contribui para o equilíbrio do ecossistema. Os jabutis, por exemplo, ajudam a espalhar sementes e favorecem o nascimento de novas árvores.

Um dos animais recuperados foi um ouriço-cacheiro que chegou ao centro ainda recém-nascido.

"É um ouriço-cacheiro que chegou filhotinho, com dois ou três dias de nascido. Teve que ser alimentado na seringa. Depois, com o tempo, ele aceitou a mamadeira", contou o presidente do Cereias.

Quando o animal chegou à fase adulta, a equipe conseguiu formar um casal para que os dois fossem devolvidos juntos à natureza.

"Chegou um parceiro, a gente formou o casal e soltamos o grupo acasalado", explicou.

Além da soltura, algumas gaiolas utilizadas para manter animais em cativeiro foram destruídas. Para Joseano Torezani, a captura ilegal prejudica o meio ambiente e pode afetar também a vida das pessoas.

"Não basta só ser o desmatamento para diminuir o habitat das espécies, mas a captura ilegal, essa pressão que eles fazem sobre os animais, só traz prejuízo para o meio ambiente e para as pessoas. É uma saúde só. Se o meio ambiente começar a ficar doente, ficar desequilibrado, isso vai refletir diretamente na nossa saúde e no nosso bem-estar."

Depois de meses ou até anos de recuperação, os animais são preparados para deixar os viveiros e voltar para a mata. Para a equipe que acompanha o processo, a soltura representa o resultado de todo o trabalho de recuperação e adaptação.

"É muito gratificante, porque a gente vê que, no cativeiro, aquela espécie em si ia acabar sendo perdida, talvez até entrando em extinção. Com a soltura de vários animais, vendo que eles conseguem se reproduzir na natureza, a gente vê que aquela espécie vai estar segura", afirmou.

Durante uma das solturas acompanhadas pela equipe, as aves começaram a cantar assim que a grade do viveiro foi aberta. Depois de meses ou até anos de recuperação, os animais agora têm novamente a oportunidade de viver em liberdade.

articles.title: Cachoeira da Velha: conheça um dos cartões-postais do Jalapão | G1
articles.standfirst: Localizada em uma área remota do Jalapão, a Cachoeira da Velha impressiona pela grandiosidade e é ideal para contemplação. O acesso por estrada de chão exige veículo adequado, acompanhamento de guia e equipamentos de proteção.
articles.summary: Localizada em uma área remota do Jalapão, a Cachoeira da Velha impressiona pela grandiosidade e é ideal para contemplação. O acesso por estrada de chão exige veículo adequado.
articles.body:
Considerada uma das mais belas quedas d’água do Jalapão, a Cachoeira da Velha impressiona pelo volume de água e pela força da correnteza. Localizada a aproximadamente 100 quilômetros de Ponte Alta do Tocantins, a cachoeira exige planejamento para a visitação, além de atenção às normas de segurança, por estar em uma área isolada e de difícil acesso.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O trajeto é feito por estrada de terra e dura cerca de duas horas. Segundo o guia de turismo e empresário Raedson Carlos Barbosa, o percurso impõe desafios aos motoristas. “Para chegar até a cachoeira, tem um longo trecho de estrada de chão. Embora até seja possível tentar com veículo de passeio, não recomendo ir em carro comum. O ideal é um veículo apropriado para a região”, orientou.

Além das condições da estrada, a localização afastada torna o acompanhamento de um profissional ainda mais importante. Segundo Barbosa, a logística de acesso é um dos fatores que contribuem para que a Cachoeira da Velha receba menos visitantes do que outros atrativos da região.

"É um ponto bem isolado de tudo e com visitação mais restrita, por isso recomendo fortemente a contratação de um guia para acompanhar o passeio. Na minha opinião, é um dos mais marcantes do Jalapão. É uma pena que quase ninguém visita", afirmou.

Com grande volume de água e natureza preservada, atrativo impressiona pela força da correnteza — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal de Raedson Carlos

A vista da cachoeira e o som estrondoso das águas estão entre os destaques da visita. “O visual da cachoeira, a força e a preservação do local são impressionantes. Contudo, não se deve mergulhar ou tomar banho próximo à queda, pois a correnteza é muito forte e há risco grave de acidentes. O atrativo é voltado exclusivamente à contemplação”, alertou Raedson.

Para quem deseja se refrescar, a recomendação é estender o passeio até a praia de água doce localizada a poucos metros dali. Nesse trecho, o rio tem águas mais calmas, propícias para o banho, desde que sejam respeitadas as orientações de segurança.

Por ser uma área preservada e com menor circulação de pessoas, o local exige cuidados redobrados com a vegetação e a fauna nativa do Cerrado.

Para caminhar pelas imediações da cachoeira, é indispensável usar calçados fechados e resistentes, além de perneiras de proteção — acessórios que cobrem a parte inferior das pernas e ajudam a prevenir acidentes com animais peçonhentos.

Para percorrer as trilhas com conforto e segurança, a recomendação é usar roupas leves e de secagem rápida, dando preferência a calças compridas e camisas de manga longa com proteção UV.

Na mochila, itens básicos não podem faltar:

Água em quantidade suficiente para manter a hidratação durante o dia;

Lanches práticos e calóricos (como castanhas, frutas secas e barras de cereal);

Sacos plásticos para armazenar e trazer de volta todo o lixo produzido ao longo do trajeto.

articles.title: Arroz de Carneiro: aprenda deliciosa receita destaque no Clube Rural | G1
articles.standfirst: A receita combina carne de carneiro, arroz, tomate, pimentão, cebola branca, leite de coco e queijo muçarela e é uma opção para almoços em família e ocasiões especiais.
articles.summary: Aprenda a fazer o Arroz de Carneiro preparado por Rai Marques no Clube Rural. A receita leva leite de coco, muçarela e temperos
articles.body:
Arroz de carneiro — Foto: Reprodução / Rede Clube

O programa Clube Rural deste domingo (18) ensinou o preparo de um Arroz de Carneiro feito pela cozinheira Raimunda Marques, conhecida como Rai Marques.

A receita combina carne de carneiro, arroz, tomate, pimentão, cebola branca, leite de coco e queijo muçarela, resultando em um prato saboroso para almoços em família e ocasiões especiais.

2 kg de carne de carneiro (colchão ou paleta);

O primeiro passo é temperar bem a carne com os ingredientes. Misture tudo com as mãos para que os sabores fiquem incorporados. Reserve parte da cebola e do cheiro verde para a finalização do prato. Em seguida, leve a carne para uma panela com um fio de azeite e alho.

Durante o cozimento, adicione água aos poucos, sem exagerar na quantidade. Cozinhe a carne na panela de pressão por pelo menos 20 minutos. Após esse período, verifique se ela está macia. Caso ainda não esteja no ponto ideal, volte com a panela ao fogo por mais alguns minutos.

Com a carne cozida e macia, transfira-a para uma panela maior. Acrescente o restante da cebola e um pouco de cheiro-verde. Adicione o arroz cozido aos poucos, junto com o leite de coco, mexendo sempre. Em seguida, acrescente o queijo muçarela.

Depois disso, o prato está pronto para ser servido.

articles.title: Novas gerações assumem o comando nas lavouras do interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovens agricultores apostam em tecnologia e inovação para dar continuidade ao trabalho das famílias e fortalecer a produção rural no noroeste paulista.
articles.summary: O trabalho no campo tem passado de geração em geração, unindo experiência, tradição e novas tecnologias. No noroeste paulista, jovens produtores assumem o comando das propriedades.
articles.body:
Novas gerações assumem o comando nas lavouras do interior de SP — Foto: TV TEM

O trabalho no campo tem passado de geração em geração, unindo experiência, tradição e novas tecnologias. No noroeste paulista, jovens produtores assumem o comando das propriedades rurais e levam inovação para atividades que fazem parte da história de suas famílias.

O engenheiro agrônomo Jhonata Yaji cresceu acompanhando a rotina no campo ao lado do pai. Depois de se formar em agronomia pela Universidade Estadual de Maringá (UEM), voltou para a propriedade da família e passou a ser responsável pela produção de alface.

Com os conhecimentos adquiridos na graduação, Jhonata ajudou a realizar um antigo projeto do pai. O cultivo, que antes era feito exclusivamente no solo e enfrentava dificuldades durante os períodos de chuva, passou a utilizar o sistema hidropônico, método em que as raízes das plantas se desenvolvem em água enriquecida com nutrientes.

Segundo o jovem produtor, o campo ainda oferece oportunidades para quem deseja investir no setor. Isso porque muitos jovens deixam o meio rural, enquanto produtores mais antigos encerram as atividades, reduzindo a concorrência em algumas áreas do mercado.

Atualmente, a propriedade conta com 150 bancadas de cultivo hidropônico, onde são produzidos alface, salsa, cebolinha e hortelã.

Em Araçatuba (SP), o engenheiro agrônomo Bruno Sobrinho, de 23 anos, representa a terceira geração da família à frente da produção de sorgo, cultura utilizada na fabricação de ração animal e silagem.

Incentivado pelo pai, Amauri Roberto Sobrinho, a seguir os estudos na área, Bruno hoje é responsável pelo planejamento, cultivo e colheita da produção.

A união entre conhecimento técnico e experiência prática tem fortalecido o trabalho da família. Para Amauri, a participação do filho na propriedade traz mais segurança para o futuro da produção, além de reforçar os laços familiares.

Mais do que dar continuidade ao negócio, Bruno se tornou peça fundamental na rotina da fazenda. Agora, a expectativa da família é que as próximas gerações também mantenham vivo o legado construído no campo.

articles.title: Uma receita japonesa para aceitar a passagem do tempo | G1
articles.standfirst: O filósofo e psicólogo Ichiro Kishimi ensina que devemos abandonar a 'lógica da produtividade' e reconhecer nosso próprio valor.
articles.summary: O filósofo e psicólogo Ichiro Kishimi ensina que devemos abandonar a 'lógica da produtividade' e reconhecer nosso próprio valor.
articles.body:
“O melhor da vida é descer a ladeira”. O título do primeiro capítulo do livro A coragem de envelhecer: como a filosofia pode ajudar você a aceitar os efeitos da passagem do tempo é, claro, uma provocação. Seu autor, o filósofo e psicólogo Ichiro Kishimi, questiona o motivo de as pessoas lamentarem tanto o envelhecimento e diz que, nas sessões de terapia, costuma perguntar aos pacientes: “Você gostaria de voltar a ser como era aos 18 anos?”. A maioria responde que em hipótese alguma. “Eles não acham que basta ser jovem para ser feliz. Ou seja, a juventude não é necessariamente superior à velhice”, afirma. Kishimi é um seguidor de Alfred Adler, psiquiatra e psicólogo austríaco contemporâneo de Sigmund Freud que seguiu um caminho independente. Um dos conceitos centrais de seu trabalho é a força motivadora que leva o indivíduo a buscar o crescimento e a superação de obstáculos.

O filósofo e psicólogo Ichiro Kishimi, autor de A coragem de envelhecer: como a filosofia pode ajudar você a aceitar os efeitos da passagem do tempo — Foto: Divulgação

“O importante não é se comparar com o outro para saber se está acima ou abaixo dele, e sim dar um passo à frente para transformar a própria realidade e evoluir. Precisamos abandonar a lógica da produtividade e deixar de julgar os outros e nós mesmos pelo que produzimos. Esse é o ambiente do trabalho, um espaço de competição no qual somos avaliados permanentemente. Ao envelhecer, devemos nos afastar desse sistema de valores”, escreve.

Na sua avaliação, há três requisitos para se tornar um adulto de verdade:

Ser capaz de reconhecer seu próprio valor, independentemente da opinião alheia;

Tomar decisões e assumir a responsabilidade pelas próprias escolhas;

Evitar o egocentrismo: “Assim como não vivemos para satisfazer as expectativas e demandas alheias, ninguém vive para satisfazer as nossas expectativas e demandas”, detalha.

Aos 50 anos, o escritor teve um infarto e, um ano depois, se submeteu a uma cirurgia para a colocação de uma ponte de safena. “Adoecer gravemente é difícil. Muito pior do que as dores, as dificuldades e os desconfortos causados pela doença é não ter certeza de que estaremos vivos amanhã”, conta no livro. E compartilha seu sentimento de angústia: “Depois do medo da morte, passei a sentir um desespero: se não for capaz de fazer nada, talvez minha vida não tenha valor. Mas, certo dia, refleti: e se a pessoa internada fosse um familiar ou grande amigo? Eu ficaria grato por ela estar viva, então percebi que o mesmo se aplicava a mim. O fato de estar vivo era motivo de alegria para os outros, o que me fez recuperar a calma. A doença pode ser um ponto de virada”, ensina.

Na sequência, Kishimi assumiu o papel de cuidador do pai, e a obra dedica bastante espaço a essa experiência. Selecionei alguns trechos inspiradores:

Cuidado sem imposição: “Os filhos não devem impor suas crenças e ideias, nem se intrometer quando não forem chamados a opinar. Devem apenas tomar decisões práticas, que busquem o melhor para os pais sem criar regras indesejadas.”

Pais com demência: “Quando meu pai me disse que se esforçava, mas não conseguia lembrar das coisas que tinha esquecido, senti que era uma lição para mim. Mesmo que eles permaneçam presos ao passado, cabe a nós dar o primeiro passo e concentrar nossa atenção no aqui e agora.”

Recomeço diário: “Se conseguirmos nos relacionar com nossos pais como se fosse sempre o primeiro encontro, passaremos a ouvir melhor o que eles têm a dizer e os trataremos com mais respeito.”

Por fim, ele nos dá outras duas lições: a importância de reconhecer quando não se consegue dar conta de tudo e a coragem de admitir quando não sabemos algo: “Envelhecer não transforma automaticamente ninguém numa pessoa admirável ou digna de respeito. Muitas vezes os jovens deixam de ouvir os mais velhos porque esses falam como se soubessem tudo e fossem grandes sábios. Frases como ‘você ainda não entende isso’ ou ‘só quando envelhecer vai compreender’ criam distância”.

articles.title: Fumaça em Manaus: poluentes persistem nas zonas Sul e Leste | G1
articles.standfirst: A especialista Andrea Ramos afirmou que, apesar de os dados apontarem dois eixos de concentração de poluentes, não é possível afirmar, com precisão, de onde vem os poluentes.
articles.summary: Fumaça em Manaus mantém poluentes em níveis críticos e especialistas analisam a qualidade do ar nas zonas Sul e Leste sob a expectativa de chuvas para os próximos dias.
articles.body:
Manaus enfrenta um agravamento da poluição causada pela fumaça, com qualidade do ar classificada como péssima em pontos da capital. A meteorologista Andrea Ramos informou ao g1 que os mapas indicam maior concentração de material particulado nas zonas Sul e Leste da capital . A previsão de chuva para este domingo (18) e segunda-feira (19) pode ajudar a reduzir os poluentes, mas não garante melhora na qualidade do ar, segundo a especialista.

Neste sábado (17), a capital amazonense registrou um dos piores índices de qualidade do ar após o agravamento da concentração de fumaça em toda a região. A fumaça reduziu a visibilidade e impediu operações aéreas no combate aos incêndios florestais neste sábado , segundo o Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama). A retomada ocorreu horas depois, após melhora da visibilidade.

Os dados do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas (UEA), indicavam qualidade do ar entre ruim e moderada por volta de 18h. Mais cedo, por volta das 6h55, os índices eram classificados como "péssimo" nos pontos monitorados da capital. Em um deles, a concentração de partículas chegou a 457,7 µg/m³, no bairro Coroado.

Fumaça cobre Manaus novamente neste sábado (17). — Foto: Alcides Neto

Andrea Ramos também compartilhou imagens de satélite que mostram que a capital amazonense está em uma região que registra a qualidade do ar como "perigoso". A imagem também mostra outras cidades, como como Borba e Humaitá, sob a camada vermelha. Segundo a meteorologista, a classificação segue um modelo do departamento de qualidade do ar dos Estados Unidos.

"Então você vê que Manaus está com um índice de perigoso. A pior situação em Santarém, na parte oeste do Pará", disse.

De acordo com a meteorologista, a chuva pode ajudar a reduzir a concentração de poluentes na atmosfera, mas não elimina necessariamente o problema. Ela afirmou que, mesmo com a melhora provocada pela precipitação, a qualidade do ar pode continuar ruim.

"Como está tendo chuva - tanto é que está tendo melhoria na parte verde quando a gente olha - Tefé ainda continua, mesmo com esse sistema de chuvas, ela faz uma remoção, mas ainda assim fica essa condição de uma qualidade ruim", declarou.

Andrea Ramos também ressaltou que a presença de fumaça pode estar relacionada tanto a queimadas em outras regiões quanto a ações humanas na própria capital. Neste sábado, um incêndio no lixão de Manacapuru, na Região Metropolitana de Manaus, foi registrado por moradores do município.

A meteorologista Andrea Ramos também afirmou que há previsão de chuvas em Manaus neste domingo (18) e na segunda-feira (19), que podem ajudar a amenizar a concentração de poluentes na atmosfera. Segundo os dados consultados pela especialista, há possibilidade de chuva já no fim da noite deste sábado (17).

Andrea explicou que a chuva contribui para remover parte do material particulado suspenso no ar, mas não significa necessariamente que a qualidade do ar voltará a níveis considerados bons. Mesmo com a precipitação, a concentração de poluentes pode continuar elevada.

Órgãos emitem alertas e orientam população a se proteger da fumaça

Por volta das 8h13 deste sábado, a Defesa Civil do Estado emitiu um alerta de risco severo para a qualidade do ar. Diante da fumaça, o órgão recomendou o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e que os moradores evitem a exposição ao poluente.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo número 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

A Prefeitura de Manaus também publicou orientações para reduzir a exposição à fumaça das queimadas. Entre as recomendações estão beber bastante água, manter portas e janelas fechadas e umidificar os ambientes.

O município orientou ainda o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e a evitar atividades físicas ao ar livre. A prefeitura também alertou que provocar queimadas é crime e pediu que os casos sejam denunciados pelo telefone 153 ou pelo site: slim.manaus.am.gov.br.

Moradores relatam fumaça intensa e dificuldade para respirar

Nas redes sociais, moradores de Manaus relataram cheiro forte de fumaça, ardência nos olhos e dificuldade para respirar neste sábado. Algumas publicações descreveram o episódio como o pior já vivido na capital.

"Mais um dia acordando com o fedor insuportável de fumaça. a qualidade do ar em manaus continua péssima e, mais uma vez, volto a dizer que sinto que estão tentando nos matar sufocados", escreveu um usuário na rede social X.

Outro morador relatou que a fumaça prejudicava a visibilidade: "Hoje de longe o pior dia pra se estar em Manaus, a fumaça é tão forte, fedorenta e densa que até a visibilidade tá afetada".

"O pior limiar de todos os episódios de fumaça na cidade", publicou outra pessoa.

Também houve relatos de ardência nos olhos mesmo dentro de casa e críticas à atuação das autoridades. "Arrisco dizer que hoje é o pior dia de Manaus no quesito poluição, os olhos ardem dentro de casa. E o pior: os governantes não estão levando o assunto tão a sério como deveria ser", escreveu um usuário.

Vista do bairro Flores, em Manaus, em dia de céu limpo e neste sábado (17), quando a fumaça das queimadas encobriu a região — Foto: Ianke Sena

Vista da Avenida das Flores encoberta de fumaça em Manaus — Foto: Michael Pereira

articles.title: 'Me senti realizado', diz agricultor que se vestiu de drag queen para realizar sonho do filho no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: João Zocatelli, de 64 anos, posou maquiado com uma peruca em atividades do dia a dia na roça. Pai e filho relatam que projeto mudou a relação entre eles.
articles.summary: João Zocatelli, de 64 anos, posou maquiado com uma peruca em atividades do dia a dia na roça. Pai e filho relatam que projeto mudou a relação entre eles.
articles.body:
O agricultor João Zocatelli, de 64 anos, diz ter se sentido realizado ao se vestir de drag queen para participar de um projeto artístico do filho, o fotógrafo Danilo Zocatelli, de 37 anos, em Marialva , no norte do Paraná.

Apesar do choque inicial ao se ver maquiado, João conta que a experiência foi marcada pelo carinho e pela reação das pessoas, que passaram a abordá-lo com elogios e abraços.

“Eu me senti realizado pelo teu sonho, né? [...] Todo mundo que me encontra fala alguma coisa. A cada pouco vem um elogio, um abraço de uma pessoa. E isso aí foi muito forte para mim. Eu ter aceitado e ter essa repercussão", relata João.

O projeto, chamado Querido Pai , faz parte da pesquisa de mestrado de Danilo no Royal College of Art, em Londres, na Inglaterra. Nas fotografias, o agricultor aparece maquiado, usando peruca e roupas de drag queen em cenários da rotina rural, como plantações, celeiros e atividades no campo.

'Querido Pai, Te olhar na sua roupa de sítio com a cara pintada e usando uma peruca enorme foi como todo filho deveria ver seu pai um heroi'. — Foto: Danilo Zocatelli

Para Danilo, os registros representam mais do que o apoio de pai para filho, mas também uma "troca de papéis". Ao g1 , o fotógrafo explicou que, por morar no exterior, quando visitava os pais no Brasil, sentia que tinha uma personalidade diferente da que tem no país europeu – era como se ele montasse um personagem ao chegar na cidade em que cresceu.

"Eu sempre tinha essa necessidade de estar, de certa forma, performando uma certa masculinidade devido ao ambiente em que cresci. E eu via que, todas as vezes que eu voltava para o Brasil, eu ia me desmontando. Eu tinha uma vida lá [na Inglaterra], uma forma de me expressar e tinha uma curiosidade, e aí, quando eu vinha para o Brasil, eu tinha uma outra", relatou.

O convite para que o pai posasse para as fotos foi também um convite para que os dois pudessem se compreender melhor. A partir desse sentimento e com a vontade de criar um projeto "chocante", como Danilo mesmo define, a iniciativa tomou forma.

Registros do pai ao longo dos anos integram uma das peças do trabalho de Danilo Zocatelli. — Foto: Danilo Zocatelli/Acervo Pessoal

O convite demorou cerca de cinco segundos para ser aceito, lembra Danilo. "Ele me disse: 'Só vou fazer se você comprar uma peruca bonita para mim e para sua mãe. Mas tem que ser com uma peruca bonita'", conta.

Ao introduzir a ideia, Danilo explicou que as fotos só fariam sentido com a participação do pai e adiantou que o processo poderia fazer surgir assuntos sobre os quais nunca haviam conversado antes.

Entre a maquiagem e a poeira da roça, as sessões de fotos acabaram indo além do experimento artístico, provocando uma transformação na maneira como pai e filho se enxergam. O intuito, segundo Danilo, nunca foi mudar o jeito do agricultor, mas sim que ele possa sentir como o fotógrafo se sente, pelo menos uma vez.

"Eu só quero, por um dia, poder te mostrar como eu pertenço no mundo, como eu me sinto. Eu quero te olhar e me ver refletido em você, sem ter medo de ser assim como sou — gay, cabelo comprido, brincos, piercing e unhas pintadas", diz Danilo em uma carta ao pai.

'Querido pai, acredito que encontramos nossa paz' — Foto: Danilo Zocatelli

João conta que se sentiu um pouco apreensivo quando se olhou no espelho pela primeira vez após ser maquiado. O choque inicial foi dando espaço ao sentimento de carinho por poder fazer parte de algo tão importante para o filho. "Tudo que foi da minha parte, eu fiz. Sem reclamar, tudo de boa", diz.

Uma das primeiras reações do agricultor foi enviar uma foto para um amigo. "O amigo é alemão. Ele só disse que, se eu precisasse de uma drag loira, era só chamar", contou Danilo.

João passou um dia tentando sentir como o filho se sente no mundo. Danilo também aproveitou a experiência para reconhecer beleza nos detalhes da rotina rural do pai.

"O meu pai é uma pessoa muito, muito sábia. Ele tem uma capacidade de pegar milhões de sementes, colocá-las no solo, fazer com que elas cresçam, floresçam, nasçam, mas tem muitas coisas que são limitações para ele, assim como para mim. Eu não sei fazer o que ele faz. Então, ver esse homem do campo, vestido de drag, em cima de um trator, com a barriguinha aparecendo, segurando um pano pink voando, é uma imagem que eu nunca imaginaria ver", diz Danilo.

João Zocatelli na fotografia intitulada 'Querido pai, parece que ir embora foi necessário para que eu entendesse que precisava voltar'. — Foto: Danilo Zocatelli

Foram cinco dias de maquiagens, fotografias e caminhadas pela zona rural da cidade. A paisagem de Marialva, familiar para os dois, ganhou novos contornos à medida que Danilo eternizava a figura do pai e encontrava velhos conhecidos pelo caminho.

O clima ao redor das filmagens era de curiosidade. Quem encontrava João e Danilo no campo de futebol, na lavoura, no celeiro, na igreja ou em meio ao abate de um carneiro, parava para ver o que estava acontecendo. Apesar da surpresa, o mais comum era que a abordagem terminasse em risadas e elogios.

As fotografias do projeto 'Querido Pai' passaram por exposições artísticas na Inglaterra, França e Bélgica. A partir de 5 de dezembro, ficam à mostra na Justiça Federal do Rio de Janeiro.

articles.title: Dog survives 50 hours alone in Alaska wilderness after avalanche; how rescuers finally found the 4-year-old poodle-husky
articles.summary: A dog named LouLou has been found alive after spending more than 50 hours alone in Alaska’s snowy wilderness, following an avalanche that swept away the
articles.body: A dog named LouLou has been found alive after spending more than 50 hours alone in Alaska’s snowy wilderness, following an avalanche that swept away the two mountaineers she was accompanying. While both men survived the incident but suffered serious injuries, LouLou disappeared into the mountainous terrain, prompting a desperate search that involved more than 20 people, helicopter pilots and a small tracking device that offered a crucial clue.The four-year-old poodle-husky mix was hiking with two experienced mountaineers near Pepper Peak in Alaska’s Chugach State Park on October 10 when an avalanche swept the men approximately 500 feet down a mountain ridge, according to People.The men were rescued and taken to hospital, but LouLou could not be found. Her owner, Lauren Padawer, was thousands of miles away when she learnt about the incident and began coordinating efforts to locate her dog.Owner launches search from thousands of miles awayPadawer was overseas celebrating her father’s 80th birthday when news of the avalanche reached her. After learning that both men had survived, she turned her attention to finding LouLou.Unable to reach the mountainous area herself, she contacted local pet rescue groups, hiking organisations, mountaineering groups and people who might be able to help. According to People, she reached out to more than 36 individuals as the search gathered momentum.“I just wanted to exhaust every resource I had and only give up I did everything I could do,” Padawer told People, adding that she was not sleeping much during the ordeal.More than 20 people eventually joined the search, including volunteers on the ground, helicopter pilots, drone operators and a scent-detection dog.The search was complicated by the difficult terrain and changing weather conditions. In the Chugach Mountains, locating a missing animal in deep snow and rugged surroundings was far from straightforward.How an Apple AirTag helped narrow the searchOne important clue was that LouLou was wearing an Apple AirTag. However, the device’s initial location estimate was nearly half a mile off, making it difficult for rescuers to pinpoint her exact position.Padawer explained the challenge in a Facebook post, writing: “On an ordinary map, that might not seem enormous. In the rugged Chugach Mountains, half a mile can mean an entirely different ridge, drainage, or mountainside especially with rapidly shifting and intermittently stormy weather.”Volunteer pilots Amanda Barker and Dave Beckett continued helping with the aerial search. They managed to pick up another signal from LouLou’s AirTag, but worsening weather eventually forced the search to stop for the day.Even from overseas, Padawer continued working to narrow down the possible location. She compared satellite imagery with another mapping application to better understand the terrain and identify the area where the pilots had received the signal.The information helped the team focus its efforts.After approximately 50 hours alone in the wilderness, LouLou was finally spotted on a snowy mountainside on October 12. The helicopter landed, and rescuers approached her on foot before flying her to safety.‘I couldn’t believe what I was seeing’For Padawer, the moment she learnt that LouLou had been found was difficult to comprehend.“I was shocked!” she told People. “I couldn’t believe what I was seeing. It was too good to be true. I cried.”LouLou was subsequently examined and found to have suffered relatively minor injuries, including a broken toe and a damaged canine tooth. Otherwise, she was doing well and had returned home to rest.“She’s amazing, she appears to have broken a toe and a canine tooth. She’s enjoying the couch and naps. Otherwise back to normal.”The owner also believed LouLou’s familiarity with outdoor environments may have helped her endure the ordeal. The dog regularly accompanied her owner on backcountry skiing trips and was accustomed to spending time on mountain trails.“She’s a seasoned backcountry skier companion dog and is very good at following the trail back,” Padawer told People while describing LouLou’s temperament and love for the outdoors.She also pointed to the dog’s thick coat as a possible advantage in the cold conditions. “I think she’s just built for cold… she’s got a soft downy undercoat and thick curly guard hairs,” she said.A rescue made possible by volunteersWhile LouLou’s survival after more than two days alone in the mountains was remarkable, Padawer credited the people who kept searching despite the difficult conditions.She particularly praised pilots Barker and Beckett for helping locate and retrieve the dog.“Their generosity, skill, and determination turned a desperate search into an extraordinary homecoming,” Padawer wrote on Facebook.For the owner, the reunion brought an end to a frightening wait that had unfolded across thousands of miles. For the rescue team, it was the result of sustained coordination, aerial searches and the use of whatever clues were available.And LouLou, after an ordeal that left her with a broken toe and a damaged tooth, was back home doing what her owner said she was enjoying most: resting on the couch and taking naps.You use AI every day. articles.title: Holy cow! Rs 20 lakh paid for a cowshed that doesn’t exist
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A cowshed that was supposed to shelter stray cattle for Rs 37.85 lakh had little to show on the ground despite Rs 20.22 lakh being paid out: no
articles.body: BHOPAL: A cowshed that was supposed to shelter stray cattle for Rs 37.85 lakh had little to show on the ground despite Rs 20.22 lakh being paid out: no cattle sheds, no borewell, no water tank, only a partly built boundary wall and an incomplete structure.Economic Offences Wing (EOW) has registered an FIR against six people, including engineers and a contractor, over alleged fraud in the construction of a cowshed at Dabhoura in Rewa district.According to EOW, the project was sanctioned under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme to provide shelter for destitute cattle. The plan included a cowshed, calf shed, fodder store, sick-cattle shed, borewell, a 6,000-litre water tank, boundary wall and land levelling.However, investigators found that officials of the Rural Engineering Services (RES) division allegedly bypassed the open tender process to favour a supplier, Deendayal Kushwaha of Chhatarpur. The probe found that two allegedly forged short-tender documents for the same work were prepared, dated Dec 3 and Dec 31, 2020.EOW said neither the tender document fee nor the earnest money deposit was paid. Although quotations were sought for 28 materials, the supplier submitted an incomplete rate list covering only nine. Despite this, officials allegedly prepared a comparative statement declaring the firm the lowest bidder and issued the work order.The alleged irregularities extended to billing. According to EOW, bills totalling Rs 27.38 lakh were uploaded on the MGNREGA portal, of which Rs 20.22 lakh was paid.Physical verification, however, found only an 80-by-25-foot partly constructed boundary wall and an incomplete building deemed unsuitable for use. Essential facilities, including sheds, a borewell and a water tank, were missing, the agency said.EOW has booked six people, including former executive engineers Rajendra Singh Dhurve, D S Armo and Himanshu Tiwari, former sub-divisional officer Jagdish Singh Rajput, former assistant grade-III employee Laxman Prasad Shukla and supplier Deendayal Kushwaha.They have been booked under IPC sections relating to criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy, along with provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. articles.title: Fr Willie Doyle: Irish campaign to make 'WW1 hero priest' a saint
articles.summary: Fr Willie Doyle was killed during World War One while trying to help injured and dying soldiers.
articles.body:
A "heroic" Irish priest who was killed in World War One while trying to help injured and dying soldiers will take a step towards potential sainthood on Sunday.

Fr Willie Doyle served as a British Army chaplain during some of the bloodiest battles of the First World War, including the Somme, Messines and Passchendaele.

The Dubliner was renowned for his courage under fire, repeatedly running into No Man's Land to carry wounded troops to safety or to comfort those fatally injured.

On Sunday, the Catholic Church in Ireland will hold a special service in Mullingar Cathedral before sending thousands of documents to the Vatican to support the case for his canonisation.

World War One had been raging for more than a year when Fr Doyle volunteered to become a military chaplain to the 16th (Irish) Division of the British Army.

He served with the division for almost two years, much of that in the trenches at the Western Front, until his death at the Battle of Passchendaele on 16 August 1917.

He was killed by shellfire while going to the aid of two wounded Protestant soldiers, one of which was a young officer from Belfast - 2nd Lt Arthur Vivian Green.

Because of that, the Catholic Church in Ireland considers Fr Doyle to be an "ecumenical martyr of charity" who died ministering to soldiers of other Christian denominations.

The campaign for sainthood is being led by the Fr Willie Doyle Association, a Dublin-based group comprised mostly of lay people but supported by the clergy.

The group was founded by Patrick Kenny, a business school lecturer who lives a short distance from where Fr Doyle grew up in south County Dublin.

"Fr Willie Doyle lived a life of great heroism and, I would also say, great holiness," Kenny told BBC News NI.

"He was awarded the Military Cross for his bravery at the Battle of the Somme. He was mentioned in despatches on a number of occasions as well."

Kenny set up the association in 2020 after he became "captivated" by Fr Doyle's courage through reading a biography of the late priest.

Born William Joseph Gabriel Doyle in 1873, the future priest had a comfortable, middle-class childhood in the affluent Dublin suburb of Dalkey.

He was sent to a Catholic boarding school in England, but returned to Ireland as a teenager, where by the age of 18 he had begun studying to be a Jesuit priest.

He was in his early 40s when he was sent to the Front as a WW1 chaplain.

Even though it was a non-combatant role, Kenny points out that the commander of the 16th (Irish) Division, Maj-Gen Sir William Bernard Hickie, described Fr Doyle as "the bravest man that he ever met".

He added that Fr Doyle was a prolific letter writer whose personal correspondence has become an important eyewitness source for historians.

"If you look at any book about the Irish in the First World War, almost invariable Fr Willie Doyle is in that book.

"Because of the sheer volume of letters that he sent home, we know a lot about what the Irish soldiers experienced."

Kenny added that Fr Doyle was held in great esteem by his own men, but was also noted for his kindness and mercy towards injured German prisoners-of-war.

There are five steps in the process to achieving sainthood in the Catholic Church , some of which can take many years, and this campaign is at a very early stage.

The Fr Willie Doyle Association petitioned the Irish Church to support its proposal for his canonisation, and the Church opened a diocesan inquiry in 2022.

"The Diocese of Meath conducted an extensive investigation - a theological commission studying his writings; a historical commission studying his life," Kenny explained.

It also conducted a "diocesan tribunal" during which experts were interviewed to determine the strength of the religious legacy Fr Doyle inspired among devotees.

"Together all of that documentation comes close to 3,500 pages," Kenny said.

"All of that documentation will be brought to Rome and then the next phase of the process begins."

This week, the Bishop of Meath Tom Deenihan was filmed preparing parcels of the evidence gathered on Fr Doyle, ready for Vatican inspection.

He said the example of an Irish Catholic priest who died serving as a British Army chaplain "has much to offer our own time when nationality and denomination run the risk of polarity".

"Indeed Fr Doyle's spirituality, and example, resonate very much with that of the spirituality of Gen Z," he added.

Members of the Doyle family have been invited to join Irish bishops at the ceremony in Mullingar on Sunday afternoon.

The event marks the "final public session of the tribunal of inquiry" after which the last documents will be collated and added to the bundles bound for Rome.

"It's a ritual that's heavily prescribed by church regulation," Bishop Deenihan said.

"The remainder of the documentation, including the minutes of the final [session] itself, will be sealed at the ceremony in the cathedral."

The bishop said it was "an important moment in the life of the Church here in Ireland" and added he was "confident" the case would be successful.

articles.title: Gym owner secures place in the Guinness World Records for most chin-ups
articles.summary: Former mixed marital artist Damien Rooney has broken the Guinness World Record for most chin-ups in an hour whilst wearing a 20lb weight.
articles.body:
A former professional mixed martial artist has broken the Guinness World Record for most chin-ups in an hour whilst wearing a 20lb weight.

Damien Rooney from Burren, outside Newry, clocked up 499 reps to beat the previous record of 495.

He now intends to build upon the record and push towards a fresh challenge for the 24-hour record which could require as many as 10,000 reps.

Damien, who runs his own gym, hopes to take on his next record attempt in April 2027.

In a nutshell Damien says a chin-up is performed with your palms facing towards you and the brunt of effort being felt in the bicep. This compares with a pull-up, where your palms are facing outwards and your lats take the bulk of the strain.

During his fighting career Damien fought under the moniker "The Rage". He says it was this period of his life which fuelled a desire to compete for a Guinness World Record.

"I've always been in and around the fitness game and during my fight career I took a full liking to the strength and conditioning element of it," he said.

He says his training was more suited to chin-ups, rather than pull-ups.

"In 2018 I first attempted the most chin-ups in 24 hours and had a few unsuccessful attempts at that through injury."

These unsuccessful attempts included torn muscles and heat exhaustion. But Damien says these are inconsequential when compared with the realities of the fight game.

"It is pretty extreme. The constant overload on the body. But as painful as this is, its very localised and very much in your control – but a really rough fight? It doesn't compare. It's night and day."

After his last unsuccessful attempt he recalibrated his training, focusing on the shorter, weighted, one hour target. Despite being much shorter, he says it is far from a sprint race.

"I think people think you'd just go out and start pumping them out but if you do that the body will fatigue and it will fatigue quickly making recovery hard. So the better way to do it is to go on a cycle where you are maximising your work but maximising your recovery in between."

To this end he broke the hour down into two minute blocks with 30 seconds of rest in between.

Ahead of a fresh assault on the 24-hour record, Damien will next take on the one- hour, unweighted challenge.

"Without the weighted jacket the record is something like 1,010 so it is night and day without it."

Those future challenges are for a different day.

After beginning this journey in 2018, having his record confirmed by Guinness is an achievement worth waiting for.

"I did this on June 1 and they told me in September. It can be up to 20 weeks because they have to go through the tapes and watch it from different angles. They are very stringent to make sure it is authentic."

articles.title: Corby metal pollution may harm people, says Earthwatch Europe
articles.summary: However, the Environment Agency says it has not found evidence that could cause significant harm.
articles.body:
Campaigners trying to examine the effects of the toxic waste scandal in Corby say they have found a presence of metals which could post a risk to human health.

Children in the Northamptonshire town have been born with birth defects, believed to have been caused when steelworks were demolished in the 1980s .

Charity Earthwatch Europe says trained citizen scientists have found potentially harmful levels of metal or metalloid at 52 freshwater sites across Corby.

The Environment Agency (EA) welcomed their work but said some metals occurred naturally and that its own evidence did not indicate "widespread or significant harm".

Earlier this year, Earthwatch Europe said its volunteers collected evidence that the presence of metals could harm aquatic life - findings that were disputed by the EA .

But this time, the group believes the samples show a potential effect on people.

Dr Sasha Woods, a scientific advisor for the group, said the results highlighted "where further investigation and remedial action may be needed".

"The findings indicate that some metals are present in freshwater at levels that could pose a risk to aquatic life, and in soil at levels that could impact human health, particularly in areas close to known historic waste sites," she added.

What is the story behind Netflix's Toxic Town?

Earthwatch Europe said its trained citizen scientists were out collecting in July, which as well as the freshwater samples, included taking 28 soil samples.

It said at every freshwater site, at least one metal or metalloid was present, at concentrations exceeding the level where "no adverse ecological effects are expected".

Nickel was found in 28 freshwater samples and cadmium was detected in six, the charity said.

A spokesperson said the comparison between its summer and winter sampling indicated a "relatively constant source of pollution; likely groundwater and landfill leachate rather than urban run-off".

"Elevated concentrations of cadmium and nickel in freshwater, and cadmium and arsenic in soil, were largely confined to Deene Quarry and a former slag heap in Weldon," the group added.

Tracey Taylor, whose baby daughter Shelby-Anne died at four days old, has spent years campaigning for justice over the scandal.

In 2009, Justice Akenhead ruled in favour of 18 Corby families and that Corby Borough Council was negligent in managing the waste.

She hoped the new Earthwatch Europe report would mean "people are going to start to listen to us".

"I'm 30 years down the line, I don't need that apology, I don't need justice, but I will fight on for the children and the community of Corby, because the Corby community always come together and they support each other.

"They should not have to deal with this or be living with this on their land. It needs sorting."

Lee Barron, the Labour MP for Corby and East Northamptonshire, said "local authorities have a duty to inspect and identify sites where contamination is causing unacceptable risks".

He urged North Northamptonshire Council - which replaced Corby council in 2021 - to publish a plan "to make these sites safe".

An EA spokesperson said it was reviewing the Earthwatch Europe report alongside its own evidence.

"Our monitoring to date does not indicate widespread or significant harm to the freshwater environment across the Corby area," they said.

"We will continue to assess the evidence and take any further action needed."

A spokesperson for the council also welcomed the report and said it would "fully assess the data and supporting information".

"Residents can be assured that any credible evidence of a risk to human health or the environment will be thoroughly considered and investigated through the appropriate regulatory processes."

articles.title: Seal pups born at South Walney Nature Reserve for 12th year
articles.summary: Two pups have been recorded at South Walney, home to Cumbria's only breeding grey seal colony.
articles.body:
Seal pups have been recorded at a nature reserve for the 12th year running.

Cumbria Wildlife Trust confirmed two pups had been spotted at South Walney Nature Reserve near Barrow, Cumbria.

The reserve is home to the county's only breeding grey seal colony and major haul-out site, a spot where seals come to shore for rest.

A record number of 14 seal pups were counted at the nature reserve last year, with the trust saying it hoped there would be "many more to come".

The pups were the first two healthy ones spotted at the nature reserve this season during a routine seal count.

Two were seen earlier in the summer but did not survive, the trust said.

Marine conservation officer Beth Churn said: "This is always an exciting time of year for us, and we hope that there'll be many more to come.

"We regularly reach double figures of pups, a trend that's been improving each year, so let's hope this season is a successful one for the colony."

The highest number of grey seals recorded to date at South Walney Nature Reserve was 563 in December 2024.

The previous highest seal counts were 518 in 2021, 483 in 2019 and 360 in 2018, showing an upward trend year on year.

Grey seals started breeding at South Walney in 2015 and pups have been recorded every year since.

"It's the result of concerted and ongoing efforts to keep disturbance of the seal colony to a minimum," Churn said.

"We work hard to make the beach safe and secure for the seals, so that they feel able to return here to breed."

There is no public access to the haul-out site at South Walney but three hides around the site let people see the seals from a safe distance.

A new hide at Groyne is currently being built and will include a telescope.

The trust is asking people to take care not to disturb the seal colony and maintain at least 100m (328ft) distance at all times.

"You can get good views of the seals with binoculars from a safe distance, so there's no need to get too close," Churn said.

"You'll know if you're too close because the seals will start to look at you and move nervously.

"If this happens, you should immediately start backing away quietly to avoid further disturbance."

articles.title: Band's new album with 'nods' to Portsmouth reaches top 10
articles.summary: The Howlers reached top 10 in the charts in several categories with its second album 'Heavy'.
articles.body:
A band's new album that features "nods" to the guitarist and singer's hometown, Portsmouth, has reached the top 10 in the Official Charts in several categories.

The Howlers reached number two in the album downloads chart, number three in the independent album breakers chart and number 10 in the independent album chart with their new album 'Heavy'.

It comes after the band's debut album 'What You've Got to Lose to Win It All' reached number 10 in the record store chart.

Guitarist and singer Adam Young said: "In one of the busiest release weeks of the year going up against some huge artists I'm so proud of how hard our whole team worked to hold our own."

He added: "It's been incredible over the past week to see how much this album already means to people.

The band spent the summer touring Germany supporting Deep Purple.

Young told BBC Introducing that this was "one of those experiences you wish you could do forever, bucket list stuff".

Young, from Portsmouth, said the band's new album features "lots of little things" on the record "linked to where I'm from", including the centre stickers on the records and the CD.

One of the songs, Cold Sweat, is a "rock/hip-hop track", said Young.

"There's little nods to where I'm from and where we were recording it and stuff like that.

"It was a really cool track to kind of write and hear the end product as well, so different for us.

"There's lots of little things on this record that are kind of linked to where I'm from and where I grew up, even the centre stickers on the records and the CD is meant to look like dazzle paint on navy ships from 50-60 years ago so there's still like a landing craft in Portsmouth which has it on.

"I kind of got the idea for like the blue and the white from that."

He added: "This record is meant to represent a step up from the previous and it's meant to be more authentic... it's a totally different experience doing this to the first one."

articles.title: How The Beatles found Ringo Starr at a Lincolnshire Butlin's
articles.summary: Ringo Starr was in a band at Butlin's Skegness in 1962 when Lennon and McCartney paid a visit.
articles.body:
A Lincolnshire holiday camp played a little-known but crucial part in the birth of The Beatles.

A young, bearded Ringo Starr was playing drums with Rory Storm and the Hurricanes at the Butlins in Skegness in the summer 1962 when Paul McCartney and John Lennon arrived to try and recruit him to the band.

Bobby Thomson, who was bassist in the Hurricanes, recalls the duo arriving early one morning after driving all night from Liverpool.

"I think that was the whole idea, to invite him to join the Beatles," he said.

"Because I was with Ringo they didn't come out with it. They could have, it wouldn't have bothered me."

He said that a few weeks later in mid August the band were having breakfast when an announcement over the speaker system asked Starr to report to reception.

He asked Thomson to come with him and the pair arrived to find a phone call from Beatles manager Brian Epstein asking if Starr would like to join the group.

Starr later recalled the conversation in an interview. "The boys would like you to join The Beatles. What do you say?

"I said, 'no, I'd love to, when?' And he said, 'oh, tonight'. I said, 'I can't', this was Wednesday, 'I can't come tonight. I'm in a band, I'll come Saturday'."

Thomson said that during the call with Epstein the drummer was told to lose his facial hair.

"He didn't want to shave his beard off," Thomson said laughing.

"So the beard came off and he got the haircut to match."

Madeline Morrison, who worked as a Redcoat at the Clacton camp, said people were surprised when the rumours of Starr joining The Beatles soon started to spread throughout Butlin's.

"Rory Storm was a big, big name," she said.

"I've got playbills where Rory Storm and the Hurricanes were above The Beatles."

She added people said he had been taken to the hairdresser: "He's got the Beatle haircut, he's joining them.

"You know, all this sort of stuff would jump round all the camps because we were all villages."

After Starr's departure Rory Storm and the Hurricanes recruited another drummer for the remaining two weeks of the summer season.

Another celebrity whose career began as a Butlin's Redcoat remembered occasionally sitting in on the drums for Starr.

Think of a Number TV presenter Johnny Ball said he would often play the first part of the Hurricanes' Sunday night performances.

"He [Starr] could flinch an extra hour on his day off if I stood in for him and played his first half of the gig," he said.

Soon after Starr joined the Fab Four, they had a UK hit with their first single Love Me Do and went on to make musical history around the globe.

Thomson described his former bandmate as "a smashing bloke"

"His personality and everything was spot on," he said.

Thomson added that in joining the Beatles "He actually made the whole team, the full set".

"We just knew that they were going to be absolutely huge."

"You were waiting for the talent to take the world over, which they did the following year."

Starr's only return to Lincolnshire with his new group would be their performance at the ABC cinema in Lincoln in November 1963.

Photographer Ken James remembered the experience as "absolute bedlam".

"The fans were screaming it was unbelievable," he said.

"The second they came on they were screaming, quite hysterical some of them."

articles.title: A Buckinghamshire wildlife garden redesigned around an unheated natural swimming pond that attracts frogs, bats, and dragonflies
articles.summary: A place where the daily swim could begin at the back door, surrounded by dragonflies and flowering plants, even in winter, was the dream of two owners in
articles.body: A place where the daily swim could begin at the back door, surrounded by dragonflies and flowering plants, even in winter, was the dream of two owners in south Buckinghamshire, who work in the veterinary sector and wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt answered with an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, bats, dragonflies, and more. Read on to discover how the design works, which plants and features support wildlife, what changed along the way, and how the owners describe their transformed outdoor sanctuary.A wildlife and wellbeing brief, how Rachel Platt connected a Buckinghamshire garden to the countrysideAccording to Homes and Gardens, which featured the project in an article by Rachel Bull, the owners both work in the veterinary sector and dreamed of a garden linked to the rolling fields and hedgerows around them. Their brief asked for a biodiverse landscape that would support wildlife while also providing space to swim, grow food, entertain, and spend more time outdoors. Rachel Platt Garden Design responded with a layout that deliberately changes character as it moves away from the house: stronger geometry near the building gives way to softer curves, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an experimental edible hedgerow toward the fields beyond. Before the redesign, the owners regularly drove elsewhere to swim in rivers and spent relatively little time in their own garden, so the new design was meant to bring that experience home.Inside the unheated natural swimming pool, a plant-free swim zone and a planted regeneration zoneAt the heart of the garden sits an unheated natural swimming pool, created as both a wildlife habitat and a place for the owners to reconnect with nature, Homes and Gardens reports. Designer Rachel Platt developed it in collaboration with Ellicar Natural Pools. The pool is divided into a swim zone, kept clear of plants and wildlife, and a regeneration zone planted with a range of aquatic species that filter the water naturally, a process the article calls hydrobotanical filtration. Around the shoreline, water mint, water forget-me-nots, native flag irises, marsh marigolds, ragged robin, and purple loosestrife add colour, seasonal structure, and fragrance, flowering from March to September and attracting pollinators and moths. Deeper-growing aquatics such as common water plantain and arrowhead offer late summer flowers and seedheads, and give emerging dragonflies stems to climb while they unfurl their wings.Frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds, all the wildlife that has moved into the garden's pondsThe wildlife has arrived in force. Homes and Gardens reports that dragonflies and bats were already drawn to the pool, with planting softening its edges and tying it into the wider ecosystem. The owners told Homes and Gardens that frogs, toads, and newts breed in all the ponds, as do several dragonfly species, and that they have even spotted a water snake. Birds also visit, using a beach area, a feature not found in conventional ponds, to enter the water and bathe safely. The owners described the pond as a total escape through every season, and said the garden has become a haven where they feel miles away from everything. For anyone planning a wildlife garden, the lesson is that a single well-planned water feature can support amphibians, insects, mammals, and birds at the same time.How drainage reshaped the plan and kept old favouritesThe pool was not always meant to be round. According to Homes and Gardens, the original concept was a formal linear pond positioned to reflect a mature birch tree visible through large French doors off the open-plan kitchen and living space. Existing drainage and a suspected utility service running across the garden forced a rethink, and the design became a circular pool. Sustainability and sentiment guided other decisions too. The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value and the wildlife they support, and much of the existing planting was saved or relocated, including the owners' fig tree, lily of the valley, raspberries, and rhubarb. Reusing what already works reduces waste and preserves habitat, while keeping familiar plants gives the new garden a sense of continuity with the owners' past.Edible hedgerow, uncut winter meadow, and autumn colour; planting that completes the wildlife gardenBeyond the pool, an edible hedge links the garden to the landscape, Homes and Gardens says, combining common hazel, hawthorn, blackberry, black chokeberry, damson, pear, and serviceberry to provide structure, blossom, fruit, and habitat. It leads gradually into the meadow, which the owners deliberately leave uncut over winter so that insects, birds, and small mammals can feed on seeds and find a place to overwinter. Autumn colour was also requested, so ornamental grasses such as Miscanthus 'Beth Chatto' and perennials such as Ceratostigma plumbaginoides and white gaura carry warm tones, while burning bush adds bright red. A kitchen garden, grapevine pergola, firepit, and outdoor shower complete the picture. Summing up the transformation, the owners told Homes and Gardens, "We really have our own little Eden," and called the redesign the best decision they have ever made.You use AI every day. articles.title: 4 years after 'The Ellen DeGeneres Show' went off air, Ellen DeGeneres hints at a television comeback: 'I really miss being on TV'
articles.summary: Ellen DeGeneres has been away from the daily television grind for four years, but she may not be entirely done with it.
articles.body: Ellen DeGeneres has been away from the daily television grind for four years, but she may not be entirely done with it. During a rare TV appearance in October 2026, the comedian admitted that she misses being on screen and has thought about making something new in the UK. She has not announced a new show, but her comments have certainly got people wondering about a possible comeback.The 68-year-old recently appeared on 'The Graham Norton Show' alongside Quentin Tarantino, Colin Farrell and Gemma Chan. She joked that she had nothing to promote and simply wanted to come and sit on the couch.“I’ve nothing really going on and I really miss being on TV,” DeGeneres told Norton.Ellen DeGeneres considers doing television in the UKIt was not just the cameras that DeGeneres said she missed. She also missed the people and the everyday moments that came with hosting a show.“I miss a lot about it – laughing with the writers and the audience. I think about doing stuff here,” she said.DeGeneres moved to the UK with her wife, Portia de Rossi, in 2024. While she has largely stayed away from a regular television role since then, her latest comments suggest that the idea of returning has crossed her mind.She also joked that getting on British television seemed relatively easy, pointing to programmes about pottery, sewing and even people watching television.“I think it is pretty easy to get on TV here,” she said.Then came a possible title for a show about spacing out while mowing the lawn: “Lawn and Order”. The remark was classic DeGeneres humour, but it was not an announcement of an actual project.Why Ellen DeGeneres left her talk show in 2022For 19 seasons, 'The Ellen DeGeneres Show' was a major part of daytime television. Its final episode aired on 26 May 2022, following allegations of a toxic workplace culture that surfaced in 2020. DeGeneres apologised to staff, and an internal investigation led to changes behind the scenes.The controversy was a difficult turn for a host whose public image had long been built around kindness and positivity. She later addressed the backlash in her 2024 comedy special, joking, “I got chickens. Oh yeah, and I got kicked out of show business for being mean.”Since the show ended, DeGeneres has pursued stand-up and spent more time away from the Hollywood spotlight. She also spoke about feeling a little bored with her quieter life in a July 2025 interview.Is Ellen DeGeneres making a comeback?For now, there is no confirmed new talk show or return date. Her comments on 'The Graham Norton Show' were about missing television and considering what she might do in the UK, rather than announcing a comeback.Still, after nearly two decades of hosting a daily programme, it makes sense that DeGeneres might miss the routine, the writers and the audience. Whether that nostalgia turns into another television project remains to be seen, but she has not ruled the idea out.

articles.title: Israel’s ties with Europe are fraying. Can its election change that?
articles.summary: European condemnation is mounting, but Israel’s election offers little prospect of a material change for Palestinians.
articles.body:
While marking Israel’s 75th anniversary , Ursula von der Leyen offered solidarity.

“Europe and Israel are bound to be friends and allies,” the European Commission president said on April 23, 2023.

That friendship reached beyond diplomacy. Israel played international football in Europe, competed in Eurovision and shared intelligence with European governments. Its weapons industry was woven into European production lines.

Those ties still exist, but have since become battlegrounds after Israel’s systematic destruction of Gaza, which has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians.

European countries have withdrawn from Eurovision over Israel’s participation. European footballers have refused to play the Israeli team. Some declarations of friendship have been recast as condemnation.

Ireland and Spain have long led criticism of Israel’s oppression of Palestinians.

At the recent UN General Assembly, Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheal Martin said Israel’s actions in Gaza “will shame the world”, while Spain’s Pedro Sanchez spoke of “condemning unequivocally the genocide that Netanyahu continues to perpetrate in Gaza”.

Recently, in a sign of how much has changed in three years, Britain, whose Balfour Declaration helped lay the foundations for Israel’s creation, imposed a ban on goods from illegal settlements, while its foreign secretary accused Israeli settlers of ethnic cleansing.

On Saturday, a group of settlers attacked European diplomats and officials from Belgium, France and Poland who were visiting Palestinian olive harvesters near the village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank. The assault, which came a day after settlers attacked a United States journalist north of Ramallah, drew widespread international condemnation.

Scarred relations between Europe and Israel may never fully repair, experts said as Israel heads to an election on October 27 that is too close to call .

Will the result affect Europe-Israel ties?

Yossi Mekelberg, a Middle East analyst at Chatham House, said if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returns with the far right, “certain things will become irreversible. The damage caused by this government is deep”.

Nicola Perugini, a senior lecturer in international relations at the University of Edinburgh, warned that the re-election of the leader, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC), would see Gaza’s population continue to struggle under “unliveable” conditions.

A Netanyahu coalition with more liberal parties might slow settlement expansion. But having a premier wanted by the ICC at the helm would likely lead to a continued deterioration of the Israel-Europe relationship. Replacing Netanyahu would not necessarily mean a break with the policies driving European criticism, experts said.

For instance, Gadi Eisenkot, former military chief and leader of the centrist Yashar party, viewed as Netanyahu’s main challenger, has opposed Palestinian statehood.

An annual public opinion survey by Israel’s Mitvim Institute last year showed that 67 percent of Israelis regarded the EU more as an adversary, compared with 14 percent who saw it as a friend.

Mekelberg sees potential for a different relationship under a more liberal government.

“The conversation with Europe would be more reasonable and rational,” he said, but warned that the picture would not change overnight.

More humanitarian aid could be delivered to Palestinians and the rate of settlement expansion could slow, analysts said. The E1 settlement plan could be abandoned.

But Julie M Norman, an associate fellow at Chatham House, said that may not be enough for European governments to make amends.

Rather, Europe would look for concrete moves towards Palestinian statehood and ending the occupation.

“But so far, we’re not seeing that under the current government and probably not under the next,” she said.

‘Ruling elite in several countries trying to align with the public’

At the beginning of Israel’s war on Gaza, Western leaders supported Israel’s campaign.

But sustained pressure from groups demanding action to stop the onslaught in Gaza and violence in the occupied West Bank – from civil rights organisations, international courts, trade unions and professional bodies to millions of protesters across the world – forced governments to act, analysts said.

“Now the ruling elite in several countries is trying to align itself with the public,” Neve Gordon, an Israeli professor of human rights law at Queen Mary University in London, told Al Jazeera, adding that the pro-Palestine movement had changed the “common sense” position of governments.

Pew Research Center polling in the UK found that the proportion viewing Israel unfavourably rose from 61 to 69 percent between spring 2025 and spring this year, from 66 to 75 percent in Italy and from 64 to 73 percent in Germany, one of its strongest allies.

Nathalie Tocci, an Italian political scientist, linked that pressure to recognition of Palestinian statehood, moves towards suspending the EU-Israel association agreement and bans on settlement imports.

“If anything has had any impact on European policy towards Israel, it is precisely the wave of protests over the last few years,” she said.

Norman at Chatham House said European states have shifted from targeted measures, such as sanctioning far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, towards “broader structures, in terms of scrutiny of the Israeli state itself”.

But support for Israel persists in parts of Europe, noted Oxford University professor Janina Dill.

Two successive German governments have been “utterly unwilling to act on justified public criticism of Germany’s diplomatic and material support for Israel”, she said.

With support generally on the decline, Israel has cultivated ties with Europe’s far right, finding common ground in nationalism and hostility towards Islam, despite historic and current ties to anti-Semitism.

Menachem Klein, a senior lecturer at Bar-Ilan University, told Al Jazeera, that the current government has caused “huge damage to relations with friends and allies” – and scars will take time to heal.

Mekelberg added that improving relations requires concrete steps towards a peace process and a different future for Palestinians. Even then, the damage will endure.

The election debate in Israel has focused on security, rather than the morality of the continued killing of Palestinians or the country’s international standing.

Israel’s wars abroad appear to have widespread domestic support.

An Israel Democracy Institute survey in April found that 92 percent of Jewish Israelis highly rated the military’s management of the Iran war. Eighty percent supported continuing the fighting against Hezbollah, even at the cost of friction with Washington. In September, Jewish People Policy Institute polling found that 72 percent of Jewish Israelis would not accept withdrawal to Gaza’s border without retaining an Israeli security perimeter inside the territory.

Israel’s diplomatic isolation might therefore seem an obvious election issue. Instead, “it is barely discussed”, Yaakov Katz, cofounder of the Middle East American Dialogue Forum, wrote in an article for Chatham House.

Rather, the main talking points are the degradation of Hamas and the weakening of Hezbollah and Iran, while the opposition promises to lower living costs, investigate the failures surrounding October 7 and draft members of the ultra-Orthodox community into the military.

“It is not that Israelis are unaware of the campus protests, the arms embargoes, growing European sanctions and recognition of a Palestinian state, and the International Criminal Court arrest warrants,” Katz wrote. “The 7 October attack has shaped public opinion in Israel to such an extent that when a foreign government criticises Israel … Israelis see only two viewpoints: that the criticism is either antiSemitic or it is ignorant.”
